You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: To what extent has the image been transformed into a pencil drawing?
node.criteria: Pass if the image is rendered throughout in a coherent pencil-drawing style, with pencil-like linework and textured shading replacing photographic rendering across the major regions. Fail if there is no meaningful pencil-drawing transformation. Unknown if the evidence is insufficient to judge. A substantial but incomplete transformation—with clear pencil-like treatment in some regions while major regions retain smooth photographic shading, reflective surfaces, or realistic detail—does not satisfy the complete condition; assess it as partial progress rather than as no progress.
node.binding: Compare the supplied source and edited images. Assess the rendering across major regions, including the food, plate, glassware, pitcher, and surrounding scene. Do not infer completion from muted color, grain, or outlines alone: determine whether pencil linework and shading replace photographic rendering throughout. Distinguish no meaningful change from substantial but incomplete stylization and from a complete transformation.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is muted and grainy, but the food, plate, glassware, pitcher, and surrounding scene retain smooth photographic shading and realistic detail. Pencil-like linework and textured shading do not replace photographic rendering throughout, so the complete transformation condition is not satisfied.

response.content: {"text":"The trace correctly notices that the transformation is not complete, but it collapses that finding into “no” despite the rubric’s explicit partial-progress category. Refine the decision criterion and binding to require an explicit three-way judgment: no only when there is no meaningful requested stylization, partial when clear pencil treatment is present but incomplete, and yes only when it replaces photographic rendering throughout. Compare source and edit for actual stylistic change, and do not treat failure of the complete condition as sufficient evidence for no. The trace is valid and has no dependency or transport failure; its high confidence does not resolve the category error, so calibrate confidence to the distinction between progress and completion."}
